label: third original token (t=2) when the second token was s
explanation: Fires only in the original phase at step t=2 when the previous input (orig(1)) was the letter s. Every such step activates (precision 1.0) and this covers 99.5% of activations. The only misses are weak echoes at t=3 in sequences like h s s ..., where orig(1)=orig(2)=s (0.1% of mass). It never fires on s at other positions, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. Magnitude depends on the surrounding tokens: the top examples (1.0 of max) are all r s o, and the lowest quartile includes h s x and c s s at roughly 0.55-0.6. That observation comes only from the examples; I did not tabulate it systematically.

issues: None of the claims fail. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.996, F1 0.998, mass recall 0.999. The dev profile agrees: activation occurs only in the original phase, never on the delimiter or in the copy phase, at t=2 (99.9% of activation mass) or t=3 (78 steps, 0.1%).

The test misses are all 75 steps at t=3 where orig(1)=orig(2)=s (e.g. 'h s s', 'e s s', 'j s s'), at 0.52-0.87 of max. There are 0 false positives. This class is real but tiny. Adding it to the predicate makes things worse (precision drops to 0.973, F1 0.986) because only some s-s sequences fire at t=3. So the explanation's account of it as a minor echo is accurate.

The magnitude claims are illustrative only, as the explanation itself admits, and I did not check them further. The 'r s o' top examples cannot be generalized: (t==2)&(prev_tok==s)&(in_tok==o) gets only 3.4% recall. Magnitude varies with the surrounding tokens, but this does not affect the label.
